Introduction: 
-------------

For this project we will interpret data from the National Parks Service about endangered species in different parks. 
We will perform data analysis on the conservation status of species and investigate if there are any patterns or themes to the types of species that become endangered. 
We will perform data clean, carry out analysis and develop visualizations as well as pose questions and seek answers to these questions in meaningful ways. 
After the analysis.


Project Scope: 
--------------

Investigate the conservation statuses of different species and identify patterns in their population counts within specific parks. We will explore which categories of animals 
(mammals, birds, plants, etc.) are most at risk and whether certain parks serve as primary habitats for endangared species. 


Data Characteristics: 
---------------------

The data spans four distinct national parks: 

    - Great Smoky Mountains National Park
    - Yosemite National Park
    - Bryce National Park
    - Yellowstone National Park

The dataset contains 5,824 total records of species, but contains only 5,541 unique scientific names (and common names).
This might suggest some species appear in multiple categories or have multiple records - different conservation statuses or common names. 

The observation data provides quantitative look at species (tracking sightings across the seven national parks).


Key Analysis Areas: 
-------------------

- evaluate the distribution of conservation statuses across the different categories 
(e.g, do mammals have more animals in endangered than birds, etc.)

- aggregate the number of sightings per part for different species. Evaluate which locations have the greatest biodiversity. Which species have the greatest sightings of rare species? 

- link the two datasets using scientific names to see the populations of species with specific conservation needs
